links.comparator_used: Static single-persona baselines applied to all cases (lean BASE_HL; safe BASE_HS and BASE_LS)
links.outcome: Safety violations, test counts and counterfactual monotonicity violations
links.effect: BASE_HL had safety violations in 8/56 scenarios (14.3%; mean severity 0.39) with mean 1.95 tests. SAFE baselines had zero violations but more tests (BASE_HS 3.38; BASE_LS 4.32). Routers had zero safety violations with mean tests of 2.14 (R1), 2.20 (R2_AUDIT) and 2.21 (R3_ARBITER). Monotonicity violations: LEAN 10/16 (62.5%), SAFE 0/16, ROUTER_R1 2/16, ROUTER_R2 (audit) 0/16.
links.tradeoff: Routers suggested slightly more tests than the lean baseline (about 2.14-2.21 vs 1.95). The simple router R1 still had 2/16 monotonicity violations. Only synthetic vignettes and a single model were tested.
links.quote: Routing eliminated safety violations while keeping test counts near the lean baseline (ROUTER_R1 mean 2.14; ROUTER_R2_AUDIT mean 2.20; ROUTER_R3_ARBITER mean 2.21).

design_hint: persona routing with red-flag escalation and dual-run audit as prompt-based safety wrapper
